# Systematic classification and naming of living things (`taxonomy`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/biology.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Life sciences (`biology`)
- Deps: helped by printing_press, anatomy_dissection, world_geography
- Core idea: Give every kind of plant and animal a two-word species name, the genus followed by a specific epithet (Homo sapiens, Rosa canina), with a short written description and a preserved specimen, and arrange the kinds in nested groups: species in genera, genera in families, orders, classes. Group by shared structure, not by use, habitat or alphabet: a whale breathes air, is warm, and suckles its young, so it belongs with the mammals, and a bat is not a bird. One agreed name ends the confusion of local names, so that a healer or farmer in one country can know exactly which plant a book from another means. Pressed, dried plants glued on paper keep for centuries as the reference.
- Pitfalls:
  - Sorting by use or habitat (herbs, trees, things that swim)
  - Treating Linnaeus's plant classes, based on counting stamens, as natural; he knew they were only a finding aid
  - Insisting species are fixed and separately created, as Linnaeus did for most of his life
  - Saying Linnaeus invented classification or two-word names; Bauhin used them in 1623, and Linnaeus made them consistent and universal
- History: greece: 4th c. BC – Aristotle groups animals by structure and notes that dolphins bear live young; Theophrastus classifies about 500 plants; rome: 1st c. AD – Dioscorides, De materia medica, about 600 medicinal plants, the standard for 1,500 years; islamic: 9th c. – al-Dinawari, Book of Plants; 13th c. Ibn al-Baytar lists about 1,400 drugs and plants; china: 1596 – Li Shizhen, Bencao gangmu: about 1,900 substances in a graded classification; americas: 1552 – Aztec herbal (Codex de la Cruz-Badiano) records Nahua plant knowledge and naming; europe: 1583 – Cesalpino classifies plants by fruit and seed; 1623 Bauhin's Pinax; 1686 Ray defines species; 1735 Linnaeus, Systema naturae; 1753 Species plantarum; 1758 tenth edition fixes animal names
- Read:
  - Carl Linnaeus, Species plantarum (1753)
  - Wilfrid Blunt, The Compleat Naturalist: A Life of Linnaeus (1971)
  - Carol Kaesuk Yoon, Naming Nature: The Clash Between Instinct and Science (2009)
